profiles.sourceReview: Primary speeches checked with ABC reporting and the Australian Christian Lobby’s distinct advocacy account. The Nightly and ABC economy stories cover the same speech, so they do not supply independent confirmation of every claim. ACL has an explicit pro-Christian advocacy perspective; its praise is not adopted. Senate page read by direct HTTP fetch after the web reader returned 429.
profiles.limitations: His WTO qualifications, existing trade benefits, religious pluralism and support for adult choice were retained as counter-evidence. Industry protection is not nationalisation; development enthusiasm is not biomedical permissiveness. Culture vs Nature estimates are especially weak.

corrections.reason: His Senate speech defends adult choices in regulated gambling. Applying that liberty argument to self-regarding drug use makes qualified agreement more likely than rejection; the analogy is explicitly uncertain and does not establish support for every drug.
